title: browser operator-journey acceptance matrix — Schedule → Topic → Script
topology: #370 fail-closed candidate lane (EXPECT_SHA, served-source, dep-lock, six-category ledger, before/after inventory, native exits); browser → real workbench → canonical /gw → exact-head stub gate API → disposable synthetic Postgres.
declared_universe: The FROZEN committed V2 surface at this exact source. Dimensions: stage {Schedule, Topic, Script} × in-stage governed action (only those with a visible rendered control) × input class {valid, invalid/empty, boundary} × typed outcome {success, denied, stale/conflict, unavailable} × reload/re-entry {yes} × cross-cutting {viewport 375|768|1280 × direction LTR|RTL × theme light|dark}. Stage ADVANCEMENT is explicitly OUTSIDE the browser-claimed universe (see PRE-01).
reduction_method: Risk-based equivalence classes per action + pairwise over (action × input-class × typed-outcome), plus NAMED three-way tuples for the risk-carrying interactions: (stage × action × typed-outcome), (viewport × direction × theme). Exhaustive Cartesian is impractical and is not claimed.
excluded_combinations: Non-#372 lifecycle internals already covered by the committed scripts-lifecycle-367 / topic-item-governance / bilingual-review-ux packs are not re-executed here (cited, not duplicated). All exclusions are enumerated as PRE-* / GAP-* rows with justification.

binding_predeclarations.statement: STAGE ADVANCEMENT (the gate commit/resolve floor) is GOVERNED SETUP, never a claimed browser control. V2 exposes NO resolve/commit/advance write path (0 matches in resolveAllowedWritePath) and renders no such control. Every stage transition in this matrix is performed as governed setup via canonical API routes and is labelled as such. No row claims a browser-driven stage advancement, and the evidence bundle must never imply one.

RECOVERY = `reopen`. `restore` (= restore_revision, version navigation) has NO rendered control in either panel BY DESIGN — ruling 1 of #373 directed recovery to `reopen` and forbade overloading restore_revision. Journeys #5/#7's 'restore' is therefore split: recovery→`reopen` (executable, see TOP-06/SCR-03) and restore_revision→unrepresentable-by-design. It is NEVER counted as passed functionality.

V2's per-item Drop/approve/request_change are RECORD-ONLY ('advances at the human commit'). The matrix must never imply V2 committed a Drop. TOP-05 asserts the record-only truth explicitly (decision recorded AND the item did NOT transition); the drop→commit→reopen loop exposes the commit floor as governed setup between the two browser-driven halves.

acceptance_rule: Every mandatory row passed; all other categories zero; serial, one worker, zero retries; native exits unmasked. Rows classified unrepresentable/deferred are predeclared and are NEVER counted as passed functionality.

rows.action: click Create run → fill days/posts/label/mix → click Plan run
rows.expected_persistence: the run is readable on a fresh browser /gw read after reload

rows.action: attempt submit with an invalid/incomplete mix
rows.expected_typed_result: typed 422 from the planner, relayed verbatim (no client-side validation invented)
rows.expected_ui: create-run-feedback shows the server's verbatim refusal; the form does NOT navigate
rows.expected_persistence: NON-mutating — proven INDEPENDENTLY: the /gw/rounds set is byte-identical before/after and no run carries the attempted label
rows.note: Observed truth at this source: the surface does not gate submit client-side; the planner owns the mix contract and V2 relays its typed refusal.

rows.prerequisite: a run at schedule_review with an absolute PLACEMENT (governed setup) — an unplaced run renders `run-schedule-calendar-unplaced` and has no calendar to navigate
rows.action: inspect the slot list + calendar and switch a calendar view
rows.expected_typed_result: 200; rendered calendar view changes on toolbar activation
rows.expected_ui: slots listed; the visible view toolbar SWITCHES the rendered calendar view (asserted via the calendar's own data-view state changing)

rows.prerequisite: a run at schedule_review with >1 slot
rows.action: click a ↓ move control then click Apply order
rows.expected_persistence: display codes + token changed on a fresh browser read after reload

rows.stage_state: schedule-open, token advanced by a concurrent context
rows.prerequisite: two independent browser contexts on the same run
rows.action: context A commits a reorder via its visible control; context B then applies its own reorder holding the now-stale token
rows.expected_typed_result: A: 200 token advances. B: typed conflict/refusal relayed verbatim
rows.expected_ui: B's feedback settles data-kind=conflict|error — never a silent success
rows.expected_persistence: NON-MUTATING: the accepted order remains exactly what A committed
rows.note: Closes journey 3's 'refusal where ineligible' half and the GPT amendment's TRUE multi-context concurrency requirement. Previously SCH-03 cited v373 R3 as its negative variant, but R3 drives a SUCCESSFUL reorder — that claim was incorrect and is replaced by this real row.

rows.action: activate Apply; observe focus during pending and on settle
rows.expected_ui: focus RETAINED on the control while busy; RESTORED to the role=status region on settle
rows.bound_test_title: R3 schedule focus — retained while pending, restored on settle

rows.prerequisite: a topic_review slot with a generated topic
rows.action: inspect the per-item panel + immutable revision history
rows.expected_ui: panel + head revision + append-only history list render; bilingual/missing-side disclosed not fabricated

rows.action: type a new value and click Save as new revision
rows.expected_ui: write-msg announced; new revision appears in history
rows.expected_persistence: head advanced on a fresh browser read after reload

rows.action: enter a rationale and click Send back
rows.expected_ui: write-msg states the decision is recorded and advances at the human commit
rows.expected_persistence: a decision by this principal persists — evidenced in-boundary by topic_item.actions.undecide becoming allowed on a fresh browser read (V2's /gw stage-state read is allowlisted for script_review only, by design)
rows.reload_expectation: decision visible; item still in review
rows.note: Observed boundary truth: SERVED_GATES restricts the /gw stage-state read to script_review; topic_review/state is refused by design, so the per-item read is the correct in-boundary evidence.

rows.prerequisite: a recorded uncommitted decision on the single open gate
rows.action: click Undo decision (gate-scoped, server-projected authoritative gate id)
rows.expected_ui: control enabled only when a gate id + this principal's decision exist
rows.expected_persistence: gate_decision removed; undecide becomes typed-unavailable(no_decision) after reload
rows.bound_test_title: R2 Topic undecide loop through the visible Undo control (authoritative gate id)

rows.expected_ui: write-msg states 'advances at the human commit' — the UI must NOT present the item as dropped/committed
rows.expected_persistence: a decision exists (evidenced in-boundary by topic_item.actions.undecide becoming allowed) AND the item has NOT transitioned — PRE-03: V2 never commits
rows.reload_expectation: still in review after reload — the commit floor is exposed, not crossed

rows.prerequisite: a DROPPED item whose decision was COMMITTED as GOVERNED SETUP (PRE-01: the commit floor is not a browser control)
rows.action: click Reopen (1:1 to the reopen endpoint)
rows.expected_ui: Reopen visible+enabled only when a committed decision exists to reverse; label maps 1:1 (never 'Restore')
rows.expected_persistence: item returns to its review status; audit records the reopen
rows.bound_test_title: R1 Topic reopen through the visible Reopen control (committed-dropped -> reopened)

rows.prerequisite: an item for which the server denies an action
rows.expected_ui: control stays VISIBLE but disabled, carrying the server's typed machine reason (data-reason/title) — never a bare hide
rows.bound_test_title: R2 Undo is typed-unavailable (no_decision) on a fresh in-review item

rows.prerequisite: a run advanced to script_review as GOVERNED SETUP (PRE-01)
rows.action: click the Script stage in the rail; expand a script slot
rows.expected_ui: Script workspace renders; slot expands to lifecycle + revision history

rows.action: enter a rationale and click the Script send-back control
rows.expected_ui: MANDATORY VALID row: the send-back control must be OFFERED and exercised — a typed-denied placeholder cannot satisfy it; if the server denies on an eligible in-review script the row FAILS
rows.expected_persistence: script_review sent_back tally advances on a fresh browser read after reload
rows.note: Hardened after Codex review: the earlier offered/denied branch let a denied placeholder pass a mandatory valid row (false green).

rows.prerequisite: a script slot whose drop decision has been COMMITTED as governed setup (PRE-01), so `reopen` is genuinely eligible
rows.action: observe the recovery control's label + absence of the old alias
rows.expected_ui: POSITIVE: `scripts-action-reopen` is VISIBLE and labelled 1:1 'Reopen'. NEGATIVE: no `scripts-action-restore` alias exists (PRE-02).
rows.note: Hardened after Codex review: asserting only the alias's absence would pass even if NO recovery control existed. The row now proves the visible Reopen control AND its 1:1 label.

rows.action: reload, navigate away to the run index and back, switch stage/lens
rows.expected_ui: durable state renders consistently; stage/lens selection is URL-driven

rows.action: toggle direction to RTL and appearance to dark
rows.expected_ui: document dir flips to rtl and data-theme becomes dark within the session; controls stay reachable
rows.expected_persistence: THEME persists across reload (pre-paint initializer). DIRECTION does NOT persist — session-only, SSR re-seeds ltr (GAP-06).
rows.reload_expectation: theme persists; direction resets to ltr (asserted as observed truth, not claimed as a pass for persistence)

rows.action: at 375 / 768 / 1280 assert controls visible+reachable and no page-level horizontal overflow
rows.expected_ui: no clipped/obscured/unreachable control; internal scrollers excepted
rows.bound_test_prefix: R4 reachability + no page overflow at

gap_register.item: restore_revision (version navigation) has no rendered control
gap_register.note: Codex ruling: recovery is `reopen`; restore_revision must not be overloaded. Never counted as passed. A future governed decision would be required to expose it.

gap_register.item: gate commit/resolve (the human commit floor) is not a V2 control
gap_register.classification: product / authority — out of browser scope by ruling
gap_register.note: No resolve/commit/advance path exists in resolveAllowedWritePath and no control is rendered. Stage advancement is governed setup. A browser-driven commit would require a separate approved product directive.

gap_register.classification: UX / accessibility — absent at this source
gap_register.note: No modal or dialog exists in V2 at this SHA, so focus-trap behaviour is neither implemented nor assertable. Focus coverage is limited to the implemented settled-only restoration + native tab order.
V2 signs a single fixture principal in an explicit dev runtime and has no login surface; negative-authority coverage is limited to server-denied typed paths, not an unauthenticated browser session.
No authored 768/1280 breakpoints exist (fluid layout); XC-03 truthfully asserts reachability + no page overflow only, and does not claim distinct responsive layouts.

gap_register.item: RTL direction preference is session-only — it does not persist across reload
gap_register.note: The DirToggle flips the authoritative document dir within the session, but SSR re-seeds dir="ltr" on reload (unlike theme, which has a persisted pre-paint initializer). Surfaced by XC-02; asserted as observed truth and NOT counted as passed persistence. A governed decision would be needed to persist direction.
